frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of ENDOWING-WITH-ATTRACTIVE-APPEARANCE: the imparting or presence of an added, ornamental layer of appeal that renders a thing beautiful, pleasing, and desirable to a perceiver. The residue is not intrinsic goodness but the applied/perceptible attractiveness — the "decked-out, made-to-look-appealing" surface — whether that surface is literal decoration or the cognitive semblance of appeal.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of ENDOWING-WITH-ATTRACTIVE-APPEARANCE: the imparting or presence of an added, ornamental layer of appeal that renders a thing beautiful, pleasing, and desirable to a perceiver. The residue is not intrinsic goodness but the applied/perceptible attractiveness — the "decked-out, made-to-look-appealing" surface — whether that surface is literal decoration or the cognitive semblance of appeal.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Three form-families all reduce to one core. (1) The noun zīnah names the attractive/decorative appearance itself or the objects functioning as such: jewelry and finery (zīnat al-qawm 20:87; women's zīnah 24:31 x3, 24:60; Qārūn going out fī zīnatihi 28:79), fine attire at the mosque (7:31), the "adornment God brought forth" (7:32), horses/mules as zīnah (16:8), the earth's decorative surface (18:7), the day of festival-finery (yawm al-zīnah 20:59), the stars as the sky's zīnah (37:6:5), and the appealing surface of worldly life (11:15, 18:28, 18:46, 28:60, 33:28, 57:20, 10:88 with amwāl). In every case the word marks something valued for its attractive show. (2) The V(II) causative zayyana X (li-Y) = 'make X appear beautiful/appealing to Y.' With a physical object this is genuine embellishment: zayyannā al-samā' bi-maṣābīḥ / bi-zīnati l-kawākib (37:6, 41:12, 67:5, 50:6) and zayyannāhā li-l-nāẓirīn (15:16) — adorned FOR the beholders. With deeds/worldly life/an evil act as object it is the cognitive counterpart: things rendered appealing so the perceiver finds them beautiful — zuyyina li-lladhīna kafarū l-ḥayātu l-dunyā (2:212); zayyana lahumu l-shayṭānu aʿmālahum (8:48, 16:63, 27:24, 29:38, 6:43); zuyyina lahum sūʾu aʿmālihim / sūʾu ʿamalihi (9:37, 35:8, 40:37, 47:14). Verse 35:8 makes the residue explicit and self-documenting: 'afaman zuyyina lahū sūʾu ʿamalihi fa-raʾāhu ḥasanan — the evil deed is zuyyina and THEREBY he SEES it as good; i.e., zyn supplies the attractive appearance that produces the perception of goodness. (3) The single V(V) izzayyanat (10:24) is the reflexive/middle: the earth 'took on its adornment (zukhruf) and decked itself out' — became-attractive. Subtracting the causative morphology (zayyana), the beneficiary/dative frame (li- = 'appealing TO whom'), the reflexive frame (izzayyanat = 'became adorned'), and the nominal frame (zīnah = the adornment as thing), the constant left in all 46 is: attractive, ornamental appeal imparted to / present on / perceived in something.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtracted layers: (a) FORM — V(II) supplies causation/agent-induced ('make appear attractive'); V(V) supplies reflexive-middle ('become attractive'); the verbal noun/noun zīnah nominalizes the residue into 'the adornment/attractive-show' as an entity. (b) CONSTRUCTION — the recurrent li- (li-l-nāẓirīn, li-lladhīna kafarū, lahum, li-firʿawn) is a dative/'appealing-to-perceiver' vector supplied by the preposition, not by the root; bi- (bi-maṣābīḥ, bi-zīnati l-kawākib) supplies the instrument/material of adornment; fī qulūbikum (48:12, 49:7) relocates the appeal to the internal/cognitive field. (c) PARTICIPANTS — the negative/deceptive coloring comes entirely from the agent (al-shayṭān, shurakāʾ, quranāʾ) and object (sūʾu ʿamalihim, qatl awlādihim), NOT the root; when the agent is God and the object is the sky or faith the same root is neutral/positive (15:16, 49:7). (d) CONTEXT — eschatological/polemical framing (dunyā vs ākhira, ḍalāl) adds moral valuation on top of the neutral 'attractive appearance.' The root itself is valence-neutral: it asserts appeal/embellishment, leaving truth-value and moral worth to the other layers.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 49:7 — wa-zayyanahū fī qulūbikum, of ÎMÂN (faith), paired with ḥabbaba ('endeared'). This is the hardest because it is (i) positive-valenced, (ii) internal/cognitive rather than visual decoration, and (iii) about a true good, so one might fear the root here means merely 'endear/make-beloved' rather than 'attractive appearance.' It reconciles cleanly: the residue is 'rendered appealing/attractive,' and faith is here made appealing to the hearts — the same operation as making deeds appealing (8:48) or the sky appealing to beholders (15:16), only with a good object and internal field. The visual→cognitive extension is not an ad hoc rescue: it is internally bridged, since the corpus attests BOTH the overtly visual pole (zayyannāhā li-l-nāẓirīn, 'for the beholders,' 15:16) and the overtly internal pole (zuyyina dhālika fī qulūbikum, 48:12) using the identical form, so 'appeal to a perceiver' is the shared abstract that spans eye and heart.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative: the core is simply 'beauty/goodness' (as in ḥsn/jml). Internal evidence arbitrates decisively against it. In 35:8 zuyyina and ḥasan appear in the same clause with zyn as CAUSE and 'seeing-as-ḥasan' as EFFECT (zuyyina...fa-raʾāhu ḥasanan): the root cannot BE 'goodness/beauty' if it is what produces the perception of goodness — it is the act of investing with attractive appearance. A second alternative — core = 'deception / false fair-seeming' — is refuted because the deceptive nuance is confined to occurrences with Satan/partners as agent and evil as object; when God adorns the literal sky with lamps (67:5, 41:12) or endears true faith (49:7) there is no deception, yet the same root operates. Deception is thus a context-plus-participant overlay, not the residue. The neutral 'endow-with-attractive-appearance' covers both poles; neither competitor does.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) ḥsn — intrinsic goodness/beauty/excellence of a thing in itself; zyn is the ADDED, perceptible show of attractiveness laid over a thing, and 35:8 shows zyn as the operation that yields the ḥasan-perception, so the two are cause/appearance vs intrinsic-quality. (2) zxrf — gilding/gaudy ornamentation; note 10:24 pairs them (akhadhati l-arḍu zukhrufahā wa-zzayyanat), so zxrf names the ornamental material/gilt while zyn names the resulting decked-out attractive state — near-synonym but zyn is the broader 'made-attractive,' zxrf the specific gilded finery. (3) jml — beauty/comeliness as static aesthetic quality, without zyn's vector of appeal-imparted-to-a-perceiver. (4) ġrr / ftn — deception / trial-through-allurement; zyn can feed these (57:20 dunyā as zīnah then matāʿu l-ġurūr) but zyn itself only asserts attractiveness, not the deceiving or testing. Falsifiability condition: the hypothesis fails if any occurrence requires zyn to denote mere existence, utility, or intrinsic worth with NO component of attractive/ornamental appearance or appeal-to-a-perceiver — e.g., if zīnah ever clearly meant 'a functional tool with no decorative/desirable aspect,' or if a zayyana clause described making something repellent. No such occurrence exists in the 46.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — 'endowing-with / presence-of attractive ornamental appeal' — is recoverable in all 46 occurrences across all three form-families (N zīnah, V(II) zayyana, V(V) izzayyanat) and all sense-fields (jewelry/finery, celestial adornment, worldly-life's allure, deeds/faith made fair-seeming). The direction is determinate (appeal imparted to/perceived by a beholder) and the reading is surface-recoverable even in the abstract cases, where the text itself supplies the appearance/seeming vector (35:8 fa-raʾāhu ḥasanan; 48:12/49:7 fī qulūbikum). The only inferential step — extending literal visual decoration to cognitive 'fair-seeming' — is not free inference but is anchored by an internally attested bridge, since the identical V(II) form is used at the visual pole (15:16 li-l-nāẓirīn) and the internal pole (48:12 fī qulūbikum), so 'appeal to a perceiver' is the shared, corpus-evidenced abstract. The root is sharply distinguished from ḥsn (35:8 shows zyn produces the ḥasan-perception rather than being it) and from zxrf (10:24 juxtaposes them). Negative/deceptive coloring is fully attributable to agent (Satan) and object (evil deeds), not the root, since God-agent/good-object cases (67:5, 49:7) carry the same residue without deception. No occurrence resists reconciliation by layer-subtraction; inconsistent_refs is therefore empty and unity is claimed as clean and universal.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 46 (19 N, 26 V(II), 1 V(V)) found no genuine failing occurrence. The candidate's chief vulnerability was a physical-vs-cognitive homonymy split, but 35:8 (zuyyina lahū sūʾu ʿamalihi fa-raʾāhu ḥasanan — adorned, THEREBY seen as good) self-documents the bridge: the cognitive family is the perceptual counterpart of the physical adornment family, both reducing to an imparted/perceived attractive surface. Hardest case = 49:7 (God zayyana faith in hearts): the only positive-valence, intrinsic-good object with a divine agent, which pressures the "applied surface, not intrinsic goodness" wording. Resolved two ways: (a) the candidate is explicitly valence-neutral; (b) zayyana is coordinated with, not equated to, ḥabbaba (endear) in the same verse — endearing vs. making-appealing-in-appearance — which actually confirms zyn's distinctive "attractive surface" nuance rather than refuting it. Festival/jewelry nominals (20:59, 20:87, 24:31x3, 7:31) and physical sky/earth adornment (37:6, 41:12, 67:5, 50:6, 15:16, 18:7, 10:24) all instantiate literal decorative appeal. Misguidance-leading cognitive cases (8:48, 16:63, 6:137, 9:37, 40:37, etc.) route the misguidance as downstream of the made-appealing surface, not as the root's own load. Distinctiveness holds against nearest neighbors: حسن (intrinsic essence-goodness), زخرف (false gilding — notably the OBJECT zayyana acts on in 10:24, so zyn ≠ zukhruf), غرر (delusion), حبب (endear, contrasted in 49:7). Falsifiable via a clear no-appeal failure condition that no occurrence meets. Verdict: unity is distinct, falsifiable, and unbroken across all 46.
